name: Simulation playback control contract
purpose: Define the future browser-visible playback controls for visual simulation without enabling simulation execution, optimization execution, delay injection execution, or operational dispatch.

research_scope.scope_note: The playback controls are designed for delay propagation visualization first. Other perturbation types remain future platform extensions and are not enabled by this contract.

play.label: Play preview
play.disabled_reason: The current platform exposes only read-only simulation artifacts.

pause.label: Pause preview
pause.disabled_reason: There is no browser-triggered simulation execution yet.

step_forward.label: Step forward
step_forward.disabled_reason: Timeline stepping is a planned UI behavior and must not trigger backend execution.

step_backward.label: Step backward
step_backward.disabled_reason: Timeline stepping is a planned UI behavior and must not mutate simulation state.

reset.label: Reset view
reset.disabled_reason: Reset is visual-only in the planned workspace and is not implemented in this contract.

notes: Speed options are present only as a future UI contract.
Changing speed must not start execution, alter results, or rewrite experiment data.

delay_visualization_bindings.dissertation_alignment: The controls support delay propagation visual inspection by showing how travel and service delays propagate through technicians, tasks, time windows, route stability, feasibility, and re-planning decisions.

validation_rules.description: All playback controls must remain visible but disabled until a real, validated simulation engine is intentionally connected.
The browser must not expose a route, button, callback, or API call that starts simulation execution, optimization execution, delay injection execution, or dispatch.
Timeline scrubbing may inspect planned states in the future, but this contract must not mutate timeline events or backend state.
Playback visualization must prioritize travel delay, service delay, and delay propagation before broader perturbation classes.
Decision response information may be displayed as a sample or contract artifact, but it must not be applied to operations.

quality_requirements: The contract must be valid JSON.
The contract must state that it is read-only.
The contract must keep playback controls disabled.
The contract must block browser-triggered execution.
The contract must connect playback controls to the simulation state, delay injection contract, and re-planning decision response contract.
The contract must preserve the dissertation focus on delay propagation.
The contract must be testable without requiring a live API server, optimizer, simulator, database, or external service.
conservative_note: This artifact is a read-only UI and API contract. It does not execute simulation, does not execute optimization, does not inject delays, does not trigger re-planning, does not dispatch routes, and does not mutate operational or experimental data.
